g12-history-uh5-t1.overview: The Aftermath and Consequences of WW II sits inside Global and Regional Developments Since 1945. Cold War tensions shaped the world after 1945, the focus of Grade 12 History Unit 5 in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains the aftermath of World War II, the war crime trials, and the founding of the United Nations. Then it covers post-war recovery and the split between the Western and Eastern blocs. Next, it follows the Cold War in Asia, from China and Korea to Vietnam. Also, it studies the Middle East and the collapse of the communist bloc after 1989. Students will also learn how the Cold War still shapes global politics today.
objectives: Describe the consequences of World War II and the war crime trials.
Explain the structure and aims of the United Nations.
Discuss post-war recovery and the North-South divide.
Analyse the Cold War rivalry between the capitalist and communist blocs.
Trace the rivalry in Asia and the Middle East.
g12-history-uh5-t1.simple:
The Aftermath and Consequences of WW II in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the huge human and economic cost of World War II and the Marshall Plan.
  • Then the Nuremberg and Tokyo war crime trials.
g12-history-uh5-t1.detailed:
The Aftermath and Consequences of WW II — the essentials. First, the huge human and economic cost of World War II and the Marshall Plan. Then the Nuremberg and Tokyo war crime trials.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe the consequences of World War II and the war crime trials.
  • Explain the structure and aims of the United Nations.
  • Discuss post-war recovery and the North-South divide.
  • Analyse the Cold War rivalry between the capitalist and communist blocs.
  • Trace the rivalry in Asia and the Middle East.
